setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The channel range is steps 1 to 4, tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and every Mosaic option is at its default. The sequencer is stopped. The Digitakt device configuration is installed next to the test device and Elektron program changes is Off. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: On channel 1's Device screen turn E3 to the Digitakt configuration and press K3. The picker shows Digitakt: this device accepts program changes.
steps.title: Choose the Digitakt device

steps.caption: In the Song editor (grid (6,8)) set Global length to 4 steps, copy slot 1 into slot 2 (hold slot 1, press slot 2) and, with slot 2 selected, raise the channel octave by one (11,8) so slot 2 sounds an octave above slot 1. Return to the Song editor and select slot 1 (1,1): slot 1 is bright and slot 2 is lit.
steps.title: Build a two-slot song

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let it run about a second, tap Play to stop, and tap slot 2 and slot 1. With Elektron program changes at its default Off, the strip below shows notes but no program change at any point.
steps.title: Play with the option Off: nothing is sent

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Elektron program changes and turn E3 right to On. The row shows On. From now on Mosaic sends a program change whenever it selects or moves to a song slot; set your receiver to accept program changes.
steps.title: Enable the option in PARAMS

steps.caption: Close the menu (K2, then K1). While stopped, press song slot 2 at grid (2,1), then slot 1 at (1,1). The strip below lists two program changes, C9 01 and then C9 00 (program values 1 and 0 on MIDI channel 10). The wire values count from 0, so the receiver selects the patterns it labels 2 and 1: receiver pattern number = Mosaic slot number.
steps.title: Select slots while stopped

steps.caption: With slot 1 selected, tap Play (1,8), let the two four-step slots alternate for about three seconds, then tap Play again. Play first sends the program change for the slot about to sound. After that each slot change is announced once, at least half a step (about 83 ms at 90 BPM) before the new slot's first note, so the receiver has time to queue its pattern: compare the program-change times with the note times in the strip.
steps.title: Hear the slot announced early

title: Announce song patterns to an Elektron receiver
